title: Mirrors, Signals & Manoeuvre (MSM/PSL)
whatItIs: The routine DT1 gives for every junction or hazard: Mirrors, Signal, Manoeuvre, where the manoeuvre is Position, Speed, Look.
keyFacts: Use the mirrors in good time before you signal, change direction or change speed.
Mirrors have blind spots: look round to check them before you move.
Signal only if it helps others (pedestrians too), in good time, and cancel it after use.
A signal never gives you priority. Stopping just after a side road? Signal as you pass it.
Habitually missing mirror checks can be judged serious: a repeated fault can fail a test.

items.title: M: Mirrors
items.text: Speed and position of traffic behind.

items.title: S: Signal
items.text: Clearly, in good time, if it helps.

a.label: Driving fault (DT1 examples)
points: Late exterior mirror check before changing direction
Signal cancelled before the turn was complete

b.label: Serious fault (DT1 examples)
points: No exterior mirror check before a big change of direction

onTheTest.question: A pupil turning left checks only the interior mirror and misses a cyclist on the left. What was missing?
options: The left mirror and the left side
onTheTest.why: Rules 161 and 182: mirrors before signalling or turning, and watch for traffic coming up on your left.

onTheTest.question: Your pupil wants to stop just after a side road on the left. When should they signal?
options: As they pass the side road
onTheTest.why: Rule 103: don't signal until you are passing the side road, or others may think you're turning into it.

traps: DT1 lists 'signalling unnecessarily' as a fault: signal when it would help someone.
Mirrors before signal: signalling on arrival at a junction, or after starting the manoeuvre, is mistimed.
DT1 also records 'using the mirrors but not reacting to the information'.
